paragraphs.text: Assignment 7
Title: Program to Implement Pizza Parlor Order System using Circular Queue
Problem Statement:

Write a C++ program to simulate a Pizza Parlor that accepts a maximum of M orders. Orders are served in First Come First Served (FCFS) basis. Once an order is placed, it cannot be canceled. The program should be implemented using Circular Queue with array.
Objectives:
To understand the working of a Circular Queue using an array.
To simulate real-world applications (Pizza Parlor order system).
To implement insertion (enqueue) and deletion (dequeue) operations.
To understand queue overflow and underflow conditions.
Outcomes:
Students will be able to implement a queue system using arrays.
Students will learn how circular queues help in efficient memory utilization.
Students will understand real-time simulation of FCFS scheduling.
Software & Hardware Requirements:
Theory Concept:
A Queue is a linear data structure that follows FIFO (First In, First Out) principle. The first element inserted is the first one to be removed.

In a Circular Queue, the last position is connected back to the first position to make a circle. This avoids the problem of wasted memory space that occurs in a linear queue when elements are deleted.
Enqueue → Add an order at the rear end.
Dequeue → Serve an order from the front end.
Overflow → If the queue is full, no more orders can be placed.
Underflow → If the queue is empty, no orders can be served.
In this program, the Pizza Parlor accepts maximum M orders. Orders are served in FCFS manner. Once an order is placed, it cannot be canceled.
Algorithm:
1. Enqueue (Place Order)
Check if (rear + 1) % M == front.
If true → Queue is full (Overflow).
Else, insert order at rear.
Update rear = (rear + 1) % M.
2. Dequeue (Serve Order)
Check if front == rear.
If true → Queue is empty (Underflow).
Else, remove order from front.
Update front = (front + 1) % M.
3. Display Orders
Traverse from front to rear using modulo % M.
Display all active orders.
Mathematical Model:

System S can be defined as:
S = {I, O, F}
I (Input) = Order request, choice of operation
O (Output) = Updated queue status (Order Placed / Served / Overflow / Underflow)
F (Functions) = {Enqueue(), Dequeue(), Display()}
Conclusion / Analysis:
Successfully implemented Circular Queue using an array for Pizza Parlor simulation.
Understood how circular queues prevent memory wastage compared to linear queues.
Verified working of Enqueue (order placement), Dequeue (order serving), and Queue Overflow/Underflow conditions.
This model can be extended to real-world applications like restaurant management, ticket booking systems, and scheduling tasks.
